module

public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Acyclic
public import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic

@[expose] public section

namespace SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- `largestInducedForestSize G` is the size of a largest induced forest of `G`. -/
noncomputable def largestInducedForestSize (G : SimpleGraph α) : ℕ :=
  sSup { n | ∃ s : Finset α, (G.induce s).IsAcyclic ∧ s.card = n }

/-- `largestInducedBipartiteSubgraphSize G` is the size of a largest induced
bipartite subgraph of `G`. -/
noncomputable def largestInducedBipartiteSubgraphSize (G : SimpleGraph α) : ℕ :=
  sSup { n | ∃ s : Finset α, (G.induce s).IsBipartite ∧ s.card = n }

omit [Fintype α] in
/-- An induced subgraph is bipartite exactly when its vertices admit a two-coloring. -/
theorem induce_isBipartite_iff_exists_coloring (G : SimpleGraph α) (s : Finset α) :
    (G.induce s).IsBipartite ↔
      ∃ c : α → Fin 2, ∀ u ∈ s, ∀ v ∈ s, G.Adj u v → c u ≠ c v := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨c⟩
    refine ⟨fun v => if hv : v ∈ s then c ⟨v, hv⟩ else 0, ?_⟩
    intro u hu v hv huv
    simp only [dif_pos hu, dif_pos hv]
    exact c.valid huv
  · rintro ⟨c, hc⟩
    exact ⟨Coloring.mk (fun v => c v) fun {u v} huv => hc u u.prop v v.prop huv⟩

/-- Computable largest induced bipartite subgraph size via powerset enumeration. -/
def computableLargestInducedBipartiteSubgraphSize (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.powerset.filter fun s : Finset α =>
    ∃ c : α → Fin 2, ∀ u ∈ s, ∀ v ∈ s, G.Adj u v → c u ≠ c v).sup Finset.card

/-- The computable largest induced bipartite subgraph size agrees with the `sSup` definition. -/
theorem largestInducedBipartiteSubgraphSize_eq_computable
    (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] :
    G.largestInducedBipartiteSubgraphSize = G.computableLargestInducedBipartiteSubgraphSize := by
  unfold largestInducedBipartiteSubgraphSize computableLargestInducedBipartiteSubgraphSize
  apply le_antisymm
  · apply csSup_le
    · refine ⟨0, ∅, ?_, rfl⟩
      rw [induce_isBipartite_iff_exists_coloring]
      exact ⟨fun _ => 0, by simp⟩
    · rintro n ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩
      apply Finset.le_sup
      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_powerset.mpr (Finset.subset_univ s),
        (induce_isBipartite_iff_exists_coloring G s).mp hs⟩
  · apply Finset.sup_le
    intro s hs
    apply le_csSup
    · exact ⟨Fintype.card α, fun n ⟨t, _, ht⟩ => ht ▸ t.card_le_univ⟩
    · exact ⟨s, (induce_isBipartite_iff_exists_coloring G s).mpr
        (Finset.mem_filter.mp hs).2, rfl⟩

/-- `b G` is the number of vertices of a largest induced bipartite subgraph of `G`.
Returned as a real number. -/
noncomputable def b (G : SimpleGraph α) : ℝ :=
  (largestInducedBipartiteSubgraphSize G : ℝ)

end SimpleGraph

findings.description: In FormalConjectures/WrittenOnTheWallII/GraphConjecture23.lean:48, the comparison with `b G` uses `distavg G M`. This is the average, over all vertices, of the minimum distance to M—not the source's average distance between maximum-degree vertices. The inequalities differ even on nondegenerate connected finite graphs. A Lean-verified witness has vertices 0,…,18: start with the path 0–1–…–12; for i=0,…,3 attach vertex 13+i to both 1+3i and 2+3i; add edges 1–17 and 11–18. Here M={1,11}, the independence number is 11, and b(G)=15. The source's average is 10, giving the false inequality 16≤15; `distavg G M=39/19`, giving the true inequality 12≤15. The induced-bipartite invariant itself is used correctly; the wrong distance helper changes this use-site statement.
findings.source_evidence: DeLaVina's Written on the Wall II, conjecture 23, states b(G) ≥ FLOOR[α(G)+dist_avg(M)/2] and explicitly links definition 26. That definition says: “the average of all nonzero dist_G(u,v) such that u and v are in M,” with M the maximum-degree vertices. Read at https://web.archive.org/web/20260726061534id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html and https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161838id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js (definition 26).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `distavg G M` in this theorem by the mean of the ambient distances `G.dist p.1 p.2` over `P := (M.toFinset ×ˢ M.toFinset).filter (fun p => p.1 ≠ p.2)`: `(∑ p ∈ P, (G.dist p.1 p.2 : ℝ)) / (P.card : ℝ)`. Document the empty-pair convention. These must be distances in G, not in `G.induce M`. Update the docstring to say “between maximum-degree vertices,” rather than “from all vertices to M.”

reformulations.difference: The source's finite-graph maximum is represented by a natural-number supremum of attainable vertex cardinalities.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a finite vertex type, the defining set contains 0, witnessed by the empty induced forest, and every member is at most `Fintype.card α`. It is therefore finite and nonempty, so its supremum is attained. In scratch Lean I proved `G.largestInducedForestSize = n` iff an induced forest has n vertices and every induced forest has at most n vertices.

reformulations.difference: The source's maximum induced-bipartite order is represented by a natural-number supremum rather than a chosen maximizing subgraph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On finite graphs the attainable cardinalities contain 0 and are bounded by the ambient vertex count. The supremum is consequently a maximum. Scratch Lean proves the corresponding iff: an induced bipartite subgraph of order n exists and every such subgraph has order at most n.

reformulations.difference: The enumeration tests colorings of the entire ambient vertex type, instead of colorings whose domain is just the selected induced subgraph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Only edges with both endpoints in the selected set constrain the coloring. Restriction gives a proper coloring of the induced graph; conversely, any coloring of that graph extends to the ambient type by assigning color 0 outside the set. The file proves this equivalence and the equality of the two size definitions; the scratch file also checks the coloring iff and finite computations.

reformulations.difference: The use site expresses CEIL using `Nat.ceil`, whereas the source defines the ceiling as an integer.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The ceiling is compared above by a natural-number forest size. For every real x and natural n, `Nat.ceil x ≤ n` iff `Int.ceil x ≤ (n : ℤ)`: both are equivalent to `x ≤ (n : ℝ)`. This iff was proved in scratch Lean, so the different ceiling codomain does not change the conjecture.

review.notes:
Checked all six declarations and all 16 direct problem use sites. No mathematical defect was established in Induced.lean's finite-graph invariants; the finding is a separate distance-definition mismatch encountered during the required use-site review. The two proved library lemmas have no sorryAx dependency.

Domain caveat: Lean drops the unused section-level Fintype assumption from both noncomputable size definitions and from b. All three return zero on the edgeless graph on ℕ, as proved in scratch Lean. This follows the same natural-supremum totalization used by Mathlib's indepNum/cliqueNum. The primary literature explicitly assumes finite graphs, and every current problem use retains Fintype, so I did not classify the off-domain default as a misformalized finite-graph claim. Clarifying this domain/default in the documentation would prevent confusion.

/workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors or warnings. It contains finite maximum characterizations, empty/singleton/edgeless/complete/cycle tests, the infinite-input checks, and the separating graph for conjecture 23. The latter uses native decision for finite calculations and was independently checked by exhaustive C++ computation. The reviewed file's hash matches its committed blob; no checkout files were edited.

The live cited university host was unavailable. Source comparisons used the archived author pages and paper. No substantiated stale repository status was found; older archive entries still marked open do not invalidate newer recorded counterexamples.
